requirement_title: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129
Type: feature

## Requirement

Given Project A (contains `ProjectA.MyType`, has no and cannot have a reference to the MessagePack NuGet package) and Project B (references Project A and MessagePack), the reporter needs a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for `ProjectA.MyType` generated inside Project B.

Proposed solution: add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that works for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

The class does not need a body; the implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

For attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), the issue lists three alternatives: (1) use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes; (2) let the generator and analyzers work with user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes; (3) source-generate the attributes themselves via `RegisterPostInitializationOutput`.

Motivation: Project A is a NuGet library that should stay minimal with zero dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute exists and can be applied to a partial class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.
- The source generator emits the formatter implementation for `T` inside the annotated class, in the assembly that declares the class (Project B), even when `T` is declared in a referenced assembly.
- The annotated class may be declared without a body (`partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;`).
- `T` needs no MessagePack attributes: without `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` on `T` the generated formatter uses contractless behaviour over public members. (derived from maintainer comment)
- If `T` does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Private members are not required to be serialized; only public members are in scope. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Project A needs no reference to the MessagePack package. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- AArnott: "We might simplistically say this only works in 'contractless' mode, such that you need no attributes on it at all. If there are attributes on it, fine, we'll use them. But if there is no `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` attribute on the type, go contractless by default."
- AArnott on prerequisite: "Does ProjectA.MyType requires only `public` members to be serialized? That seems a prerequisite for anything here." Reporter: yes.
- AArnott is not a fan of a `PropertyKeys` dictionary on the formatter, and warns that copying attributes into Project A breaks reflection-based (dynamic resolver) mode.
- AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.

findings.claim: MessagePack attributes already present on the referenced data type are not honored. With no surrogate, the collector unconditionally calls CreateContractlessMembers and never inspects MessagePackObjectAttribute, KeyAttribute, or IgnoreMemberAttribute on T. Thus a [MessagePackObject] type with integer keys and ignored members is emitted as a name-keyed contractless map including those ignored members, contrary to the acceptance criteria.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedMessagePackFormatterReceiptTests.MessagePackAttributesOnReferencedTypeAreHonored. It compiles a referenced ProjectA type with [MessagePackObject], [Key(0)], and [IgnoreMember], then requires the generated formatter to use array-key serialization and omit the ignored member. The current contractless map implementation fails those assertions.

findings.claim: The required bodyless declaration form is not supported. Generation is only registered for ClassDeclarationSyntax nodes, while a declaration such as 'partial class MyObjectFormatter : IMessagePackFormatter<ProjectA.MyObject>;' is rejected by the supported C# syntax with missing-body compiler errors. The implementation and documentation only support an empty '{ }' body, despite the acceptance criterion explicitly allowing the semicolon form.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedMessagePackFormatterReceiptTests.BodylessPartialFormatterClassIsSupported. Its ProjectB input uses exactly the required semicolon-terminated partial formatter declaration and asserts error-free generation and compilation; it fails with compiler syntax/body errors under the current implementation.

hunches.claim: The security fallback for types that are not explicitly approved as hash-collision resistant now returns EqualityComparer<T>.Default instead of throwing. An untrusted payload can therefore populate a hash-based collection using a custom key type with colliding or attacker-controlled hashes, regressing the stated hash-collision protection. This runtime security change is also unrelated to the requested source-generation feature.

receipt_plan.detail: Add or run a MessagePack runtime security test that deserializes an untrusted hash-based collection whose key type is not on the hash-resistant whitelist and whose equality comparer produces colliding hashes. The base behavior should throw TypeAccessException at this fallback; the head behavior proceeds with EqualityComparer<T>.Default, demonstrating the regression.

hunches.claim: MessagePack attributes on the formatted type are ignored. With no surrogate, Collect always calls CreateContractlessMembers, which includes every public read-write member under name-based string keys without inspecting MessagePackObject, Key, or IgnoreMember. A referenced type annotated with [Key(0)] and [IgnoreMember] therefore gets the wrong wire format, directly violating the acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes on T be honoured.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile ProjectA.MyObject into a metadata reference with [MessagePackObject], [Key(0)] on Value, and [IgnoreMember] on Ignored. Generate a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class in Project B and inspect the emitted partial formatter: it should use ReadArrayHeader for the integer-key contract and should not access Ignored. On head it instead emits a string-key formatter containing both members.

hunches.claim: The fallback for key types without an explicitly registered hash-resistant comparer now returns EqualityComparer<T>.Default instead of throwing. Untrusted hash-based collection deserialization consequently accepts arbitrary custom key types with potentially collision-prone hashes, enabling the hash-collision denial-of-service attack that this guard and its adjacent comment exist to prevent.

receipt_plan.detail: Expose MessagePackSecurity.GetHashCollisionResistantEqualityComparer<T> through a test subclass and invoke it for a non-whitelisted custom key type, or deserialize a hash-based collection with that key type using MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData. The existing security contract requires TypeAccessException; head returns/uses the default equality comparer instead.

hunches.claim: MessagePack attributes on T are not honoured: when no surrogate is supplied, the collector always builds a contractless string-key model, ignoring [MessagePackObject], [Key], and [IgnoreMember] on T. A generated formatter for an attributed type therefore uses different member membership and wire keys instead of its declared MessagePack contract.

receipt_plan.detail: Define ProjectA.MyType as [MessagePackObject] public class MyType { [Key(0)] public int A { get; set; } [Key(1)] public string B { get; set; } [IgnoreMember] public int Ignored { get; set; } }. In Project B declare [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] public partial class MyTypeFormatter : IMessagePackFormatter<MyType>. Serialize new MyType { A = 1, B = "x", Ignored = 9 } with the existing/base formatter for MyType and with the head-generated MyTypeFormatter, then compare bytes. The head output uses string keys "A"/"B" and also includes "Ignored", rather than the expected integer-key map containing only keys 0 and 1.

hunches.claim: The fallback for key types without a known hash-resistant comparer now returns EqualityComparer<T>.Default instead of throwing. Consequently, MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData permits hash-based collections with unapproved key types and loses its hash-collision denial-of-service protection; an attacker can supply colliding keys to force pathological dictionary lookups.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a regression test that deserializes a Dictionary or HashSet whose key element type has no whitelisted collision-resistant comparer using options.WithSecurity(MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData). The test should expect TypeAccessException (the prior secure behavior); on this change deserialization instead reaches EqualityComparer<T>.Default. A key type with a constant GetHashCode can additionally demonstrate that attacker-controlled collisions are accepted.

hunches.claim: The new collector always selects surrogate mode or collects all public read-write members contractlessly; it never checks T for [MessagePackObject]/[DataContract] or reads its [Key]/[IgnoreMember] annotations. Consequently, an attributed T does not have its declared keys and membership honoured, violating an explicit acceptance criterion.

receipt_plan.detail: Generate a formatter for a type carrying [MessagePackObject] with integer [Key] values and an [IgnoreMember] member, without setting SurrogateType. Serialize it and assert the generated formatter uses those integer keys and omits the ignored member; the current implementation instead emits contractless string-keyed public members.

hunches.claim: An unrelated change replaces the fail-closed guard for hash-based collections of non-whitelisted key types with EqualityComparer<T>.Default. Untrusted MessagePack can therefore reach an arbitrary type's non-collision-resistant GetHashCode implementation, re-enabling hash-collision denial of service that this method explicitly exists to prevent.

receipt_plan.detail: Under MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData, deserialize a hash-based collection whose key type is not whitelisted and assert TypeAccessException is thrown without invoking that type's GetHashCode. The changed fallback instead permits the default comparer and the test fails.

hunches.claim: The acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes on T are honoured has no test. Every execution-test T is explicitly attribute-free, so the collector's unconditional contractless path for a null surrogate is never challenged with [MessagePackObject], [Key], or [IgnoreMember] on T.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an execution test whose external T has [MessagePackObject] with non-sequential [Key] values and an [IgnoreMember] member, then generate its formatter without SurrogateType and assert the serialized keys and membership. It fails with the current CreateContractlessMembers(type) path, which uses string-name keys and all public read-write members.

hunches.claim: The body-less declaration form explicitly required by the feature is not exercised: all three attributed formatter declarations in the execution tests have braces, and all generator-test declarations do too. A regression in discovery or emission for `partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;` would pass every added test.

receipt_plan.detail: Declare one execution-test formatter as `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] public partial class ExternalPersonFormatter : IMessagePackFormatter<ExternalPerson>;` with no body and retain its round-trip and resolver-registration assertions; compilation/generation and those assertions should fail if body-less support regresses.

hunches.claim: No added test covers a surrogate member matching an existing target that is non-public or not read-write. Consequently, removing the public-read-write guard would not be caught by either surrogate diagnostic test, which covers only a missing name and a type mismatch.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:177 remove-guard: `target is null || !IsPublicReadWrite(target) || !SymbolEqualityComparer.Default.Equals(GetMemberType(target), GetMemberType(surrogateMember))` -> `target is null || !SymbolEqualityComparer.Default.Equals(GetMemberType(target), GetMemberType(surrogateMember))`; expected to survive because no test gives a same-name, same-type private, read-only, or write-only target member and expects MsgPack022.

hunches.claim: Duplicate surrogate keys are untested, so the uniqueness check can be removed without affecting any added test. The surrogate tests cover mixed key kinds, missing members, and mismatched types, but not two members carrying the same integer or string key.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:188 remove-guard: delete `if (!claimedKeys.Add(key)) { ... return null; }`; expected to survive because no test uses duplicate surrogate keys or expects MsgPack006 for this collector.

hunches.claim: The surrogate path's missing-or-invalid-Key guard has no negative test. The only unkeyed surrogate member in the tests is ignored, so removing the guard for an ordinary unannotated surrogate member would go unnoticed.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:160 remove-guard: remove `if (key is not (int or string)) { ... return null; }`; expected to survive because every non-ignored surrogate member in the added tests has a valid integer or string [Key].

hunches.claim: The security change replacing the untrusted-data exception with EqualityComparer<T>.Default has no accompanying test, so the added tests would all pass if hash-collision protection were silently disabled.

receipt_plan.detail: Run/add a MessagePackSecurity test requesting a hash-resistant comparer under UntrustedData for a type outside the whitelist and assert TypeAccessException; the current changed line instead returns EqualityComparer<T>.Default, so the test fails and catches the security regression.

hunches.claim: suppressed by unconfirmed context entry: [L11] area=analyzer, generator: Types that come from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly. In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. (source: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:367) (would-be finding: The pre-existing blanket rule that metadata-only types receive no formatter remains deliberate for ordinary discovery. The new feature is an explicit opt-in exception through GeneratedFormatterCollector rather than a reason to remove or flag TypeCollector's metadata early return.)

receipt_plan.detail: [L11] records that referenced-assembly types deliberately receive no analysis or formatter through ordinary TypeCollector discovery; REQ-2129 separately requires the explicit [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] opt-in path.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Add the marker attribute with an optional SurrogateType property so Project B can supply MessagePack-specific keys and settings on a surrogate type mapped to T by property name. Code: In addition to basic formatter generation, the generator must resolve and validate the surrogate, read its MessagePack annotations, and apply them to T's corresponding properties; the attribute gains a public Type-valued SurrogateType surface.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Add only the marker attribute and generate a bodyless partial formatter, using contractless public-member serialization by default and honoring DataContract or MessagePack metadata already present on T, without adding any new configuration mechanism. Code: The public API contains GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute without SurrogateType; key and union customization is limited to metadata already on T (including DataMember and related attributes), and user-defined attribute copies receive no special recognition.
